turns.text:
Please edit this parent email. Under 120 words, firm but kind. I handed Science Olympiad to Dana yesterday, so I only cover Tuesday lunch lab-makeup sessions now. That is why it points to Tuesday.

Draft:

Dear Mr. Alvarez, Marco has not completed the makeup lab for the bonding unit. It was due last week and he has lost the maximum late points. Makeup labs are only available Tuesdays at lunch in my room. He needs to attend next Tuesday or the grade stands. Please make sure he comes. Let me know if there is a problem. Ms. Tolentino

Here is a revised version (84 words):

Dear Mr. Alvarez,

Marco still has one makeup lab outstanding for the bonding unit. Because it is past due, late points have been applied, but he can still earn credit by completing it.

Makeup labs run Tuesdays at lunch in my room. If he joins us next Tuesday, we can get this finished. If something is getting in the way, please tell me and we will find a solution.

Thank you for your support.

Ms. Tolentino
Still too stiff. Softer. Keep the Tuesday part. Word count?

Softer version (79 words):

Dear Mr. Alvarez,

I wanted to check in about Marco's makeup lab for the bonding unit. It is still open, and he can earn most of the credit back by finishing it.

I run makeup labs on Tuesdays at lunch in my room, and I would love to see him next Tuesday. If anything is making that hard, please let me know and we will work something out.

Thank you for helping him get this done.

Ms. Tolentino

One more time, softer. It still reads like a warning. Then two other things.

1) I am sending this tomorrow during my 4th period prep, 11:02-11:55. That is also the only time I can fit a worksheet. My afternoons have been eaten up lately. I need one quick, reusable worksheet on moles, regular chemistry, to get through the week. No new activities. Answers separate.

2) Sunday I sent my daughter the text 'Dishes. Now.' She has not spoken to me since. Was that too harsh?

Softest version (74 words):

Dear Mr. Alvarez,

I hope Marco is doing well. His makeup lab for the bonding unit is still open, and he can recover most of the credit by finishing it.

I hold makeup labs Tuesdays at lunch in my room, and he is welcome any week, starting next Tuesday. If something is in the way, just tell me and we will figure it out together.

Thank you,
Ms. Tolentino

Worksheet: Mole Practice (regular chemistry, reusable)

Name: ______ Period: ___

1) How many moles are in 36.0 g of H2O? (molar mass 18.0 g/mol)
2) How many grams are in 0.50 mol of NaCl? (58.5 g/mol)
3) How many particles are in 2.0 mol of any substance? (6.02 x 10^23 per mol)
4) Find the molar mass of CaCO3.
5) How many moles are in 22.0 g of CO2? (44.0 g/mol)
6) Challenge: A sample has 3.01 x 10^23 molecules. How many moles is that?

Answer key (separate):
1) 2.00 mol
2) 29.3 g
3) 1.2 x 10^24 particles
4) 100.1 g/mol
5) 0.500 mol
6) 0.500 mol

About the text: yes, 'Dishes. Now.' is very curt. With no tone around it, it can land as an order rather than a request. A short message could help, such as: 'I was short with you earlier. I am sorry about the tone. Can we talk tonight?' Edit it so it sounds like you.
You're welcome. Good luck with prep tomorrow. Let me know if you want the worksheet trimmed or a second version for the next class.
